method: Manual visual inspection of actual XCTest captures, compared with source and harmony references plus exact native string/fret assertions. Generated contact sheets are inspection aids, not upload images.
findings: Notation and tab are legible in reviewed frames, chord voicings show distinct strings.
Old Restart captures retained the end of the staff despite a zero clock; fixed by waiting for alphaTab cursor animation-frame updates. New Amazing Grace restart capture confirms beginning staff.
Left-handed open-string markers were obscured by the expand button; moved to the Songbook header and confirmed unobstructed in all 40 post-fix iPhone control captures.
Old 97-percent slider gestures reached the completed score, correctly clearing sounding notes. Additional ending captures use an earlier seek.

All 40 initial iPad arrangements reviewed at beginning, middle, ending and every changed chord. Pitches, tab and voiced string positions agree; long-score seek/restart cursor scrolling is rechecked in the final post-fix captures.
captureBasis: Initial all-arrangement/every-chord-change review plus post-fix all-arrangement ending/restart review; final strict run 18 images retained. Not every final repeated chord contact sheet was re-reviewed.

notes: Manually inspected ending-seek and restart frames for both arrangements of every song on both devices.
Restart returns the staff to the opening event; long-score ending seeks keep the active staff region visible.
All red chord markers occupy the authored distinct strings, including open strings and the small F shape. Blue markers indicate upcoming positions, not additional sounding notes.
The left-handed iPhone expand control is outside the board and no longer obscures open strings.
Ending captures are seeks near the ending phrase, not a claim to have heard the complete performance.
